newsitem.title: USA: Albright to make nine stops on Europe, Asia tour.
newsitem.headline: Albright to make nine stops on Europe, Asia tour.

text.p: New U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will visit nine European and Asian capitals, including Beijing, next month on her first overseas trip in her new post, the State Department said on Monday.
Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said that Albright would go to Rome, Bonn, Paris, Brussels, London, Moscow, Seoul, Tokyo and Beijing on the trip from Feb. 15 to 25.

U.S. secretaries of state usually make their first trips to Europe. But Albright, an expert on Europe, included Asia to emphasise the importance Washington gives to that region and to acquaint herself with an area with which she is not as familiar.
Burns said the decision to go to both continents "reflects fundamental national interests" of the United States in Europe and Asia.

Speaking at a regular State Department news conference, Burns said the dates of the trip would be Rome February 15/16, Bonn 16/17, Paris 17/18, Brussels 18, London 18/19, Moscow 19/20 (Flying to Seoul with a refuelling stopover in Russia 21), Seoul 22/23, Tokyo 23/24 and Beijing 24/25.

Albright, who was sworn in on Jan. 23, was also scheduled to travel to Houston, Texas, this Friday and Saturday. In Houston, she will meet with Mexican Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria Trevino, former President George Bush and former Secretary of State James Baker.
